fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with tall reflective posts on both sides to improve visibility during night or low-visibility operations.
• Post the property address at the entrance to the access drive, not only at the residence, to reduce search time on a long driveway.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles traveling to and from the residence.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of fallen branches, debris, or parked vehicles that could block a responding unit.
• Identify and mark a designated turnaround area near the residence so drivers of large emergency vehicles know where to reposition without backing blind.
• Grade or mark a secondary pullout area along the access drive to allow two vehicles to pass if multiple units respond simultaneously.
• Trim tree canopies overhanging the access drive to provide vertical clearance for ladder trucks and tall emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation surrounding the detached structure to keep a clear path around it for responders on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can move between the two structures without obstruction.
• Install a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence, detached structure, and any water shut-offs

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls and foundation.
• Thin the scattered trees around the house so their canopies are not touching each other or overhanging the roof.
• Remove woody debris such as fallen branches, logs, and brush piles from the ground near the house.
• Clear dead and dry grass from the area immediately surrounding the house.
• Separate shrub groupings near the house so there are visible open gaps between them and the structure.
• Mow or cut down dry grass along both sides of the driveway to reduce continuous ground-level vegetation along the travel path.
• Trim tree branches that hang over or close to the driveway to keep the full width and height of the lane open.
• Remove any woody debris that has collected along the driveway edges.
• Keep the areas between scattered tree groupings open by removing shrubs or brush that connect one grouping to another near the house.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees closest to the house up to a height visible from ground level to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Remove dead shrub material and dry grass from around any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Keep all secondary access routes clear of overhanging vegetation and debris so they remain passable.
